site.title: Kelly Art Photography
site.tagline: Welcome to my photography portfolio, a collection of images, ideas and ongoing projects inspired by the landscapes and places I love to explore. I hope you enjoy taking a stroll through the galleries and discovering some of my current work. Your thoughts, observations and constructive comments are always welcome, as they help me develop my photography and see familiar subjects from a different perspective. Feel free to email me with any comments and requests for images.
site.featuredIntro: Special captured moments in time on my travels

albums.title: Blea Tarn
albums.blurb: A small, still tarn cradled beneath the Langdale Pikes. Everyone can get out into the fells safely on this gentle out-and-back trail. Enjoy brilliant mountain views of the Langdale Pikes and other surrounding peaks, framed by the peaceful tarn – and all without the big climbs and rocky scrambles.

photos.caption: Pikes above the tarn
photos.story: Classic shot featuring the Langdale Pikes

albums.title: Buttermere
albums.blurb: Lakeshore paths, mist and mirror-still water in the western fells. Buttermere is one of the Lake District’s most beautiful and photogenic landscapes, surrounded by dramatic fells, peaceful woodland and the still waters of the lake. Its ever-changing weather and light create wonderful opportunities for photography, from misty mornings and atmospheric reflections to dramatic skies and rich autumn colours. Whatever the season, Buttermere offers a landscape of natural beauty and endless photographic inspiration.

photos.caption: Framed by lakeside trees
photos.story: A sense of depth here framing the water with two grand trees

albums.title: Derwent Water
albums.blurb: Keswick's lake, bridges and soft valley light.

albums.title: Elterwater & Langdale
albums.blurb: Reed-fringed water beneath the Langdale Pikes.Nestled in the heart of the Langdale Valley, Elterwater is a beautiful and peaceful location surrounded by some of the Lake District’s most dramatic scenery. The tranquil river, ancient woodland, stone cottages and towering fells provide a wealth of photographic opportunities, while the constantly changing light and weather can transform the landscape from soft and atmospheric to bold and dramatic. It is a place that rewards patience, exploration and a keen eye for the beauty in every season.

albums.title: Grasmere
albums.blurb: Grasmere is one of the Lake District’s most enchanting locations, where a peaceful lake sits beneath a dramatic amphitheatre of surrounding fells. Its calm waters, winding shoreline and ever-changing light provide wonderful opportunities for landscape photography throughout the year. The village itself has a rich history, with roots stretching back to the early medieval period, and is famously associated with the poet William Wordsworth, who made his home at nearby Dove Cottage in 1799 and drew much of his inspiration from the beauty of the surrounding landscape.

photos.caption: Golden hour
photos.story: Wow reminds me of a Turner painting

albums.title: Haweswater
albums.blurb: A remote reservoir valley, wide skies and rock shorelines.  Haweswater Reservoir lies in one of the Lake District’s most remote and atmospheric valleys, surrounded by rugged fells and dramatic open landscapes. Created in the 1930s to provide water for Manchester, the reservoir now forms a striking part of the landscape, with its winding shoreline and towering mountains offering endless opportunities for photography. Changing weather, mist, reflections and seasonal light can transform Haweswater from a tranquil scene into a dramatic and evocative landscape.

albums.title: Loughrigg Fell
albums.blurb: Loughrigg Fell is a photographer’s paradise, offering some of the most spectacular panoramic views in the Lake District from its summit. With Windermere, Rydal Water, Grasmere and the surrounding fells stretching out below, the ever-changing light and weather create endless opportunities for dramatic landscape photography. From misty mornings to golden evening light, Loughrigg rewards every visit with a new perspective and an unforgettable view.

photos.caption: Path above Rydal, black and white

albums.title: Lake District
albums.blurb: A few more favourites from around the valleys.

albums.title: Rydal Water
albums.blurb: A small lake between Grasmere and Ambleside, quiet and wooded.  Rydal Water is one of the Lake District’s most tranquil and photogenic lakes, tucked between the villages of Ambleside and Grasmere beneath the rugged slopes of Loughrigg Fell. Its peaceful waters, wooded shoreline and surrounding mountains create a wonderfully atmospheric setting for photography, particularly when mist, reflections and soft light transform the landscape. Rich in literary history and closely associated with William Wordsworth, Rydal Water combines natural beauty with a timeless sense of place.

albums.title: Tarn Hows
albums.blurb: Tarn Hows is one of the Lake District’s most celebrated and photogenic landscapes, with its tranquil waters surrounded by woodland and magnificent mountain scenery. The reflections across the tarn, particularly in the early morning or evening light, create wonderful opportunities for atmospheric landscape photography. Whether captured beneath dramatic skies, in autumn colour or shrouded in mist, Tarn Hows offers a timeless beauty that makes it a favourite location for photographers. A National Trust beauty spot of pine, water and mist.

albums.title: Thirlmere
albums.blurb: A dramatic reservoir valley with waterfalls and autumn colour. Thirlmere is one of the Lake District’s most dramatic and atmospheric lakes, stretching beneath the towering slopes of Helvellyn and the surrounding fells. Its long, tranquil waters, wooded shores and rugged mountain backdrop provide endless opportunities for landscape photography, particularly when the weather brings mist, reflections or dramatic skies. With its ever-changing mood and spectacular scenery, Thirlmere is a truly inspiring location for any photographer exploring the Lake District.

albums.title: Ullswater
albums.blurb: Haweswater is one of the Lake District’s most dramatic and remote landscapes, where the vast reservoir winds through a rugged valley surrounded by imposing fells. The changing light, shifting weather and atmospheric mist create an ever-changing scene, making it a particularly rewarding location for landscape photography. From quiet reflections on the water to dramatic views across the surrounding mountains, Haweswater offers a sense of wilderness and solitude that is difficult to find elsewhere in the Lake District.

albums.title: Northumberland
albums.blurb: The Northumberland coast is a dream location for photography, offering dramatic castles, sweeping beaches, rugged dunes and vast open skies. From the iconic silhouette of Bamburgh Castle to the atmospheric ruins of Dunstanburgh and the wildlife-rich Farne Islands, every stretch of coastline offers something different. The ever-changing light, tides and weather create endless opportunities for capturing powerful landscapes and memorable images throughout the year.

albums.title: Black and White
albums.blurb: Black and white photography strips an image back to its essential elements, allowing light, shadow, texture, shape and composition to take centre stage. Free from the distraction of colour, it can reveal mood, emotion and atmosphere in a uniquely powerful way, transforming both dramatic landscapes and everyday moments into timeless and expressive images.

albums.title: Spring Wood Whalley
albums.blurb: Much lauded for its bluebell & ransom displays, this semi-natural ancient woodland is one of the best examples in Lancashire and has Biological Heritage status. There is an access for all route, one leading to the centre of the wood, suitable for buggies and trampers, and a steeper path, climbing to the summit via the arboretum. Highly recommended for woodland enthusiasts or those who just enjoy listening to Warblers, Jays and Chiffchaffs whilst eating ice cream and watching squirrels feeding

albums.title: Panorama
albums.blurb: My panoramic series explores the unique potential of the wide-format image, capturing landscapes in a way that reflects the scale and grandeur of the scene as experienced in person. By bringing together a wider field of view, panoramics allow sweeping compositions, dramatic skies and subtle details to work together, creating images that draw the viewer into the landscape and offer a greater sense of place.

albums.title: Bluebells
albums.blurb: Bluebells in Spring Woods in Whalley is a magical place to photograph in spring, when the woodland floor is transformed into a carpet of vibrant bluebells. The soft light filtering through the trees, combined with the delicate flowers and ancient woodland atmosphere, creates endless opportunities for peaceful and atmospheric images. It is a wonderful example of how nature can create its own beautiful photographic compositions.

albums.title: The Lone Tree
albums.blurb: The lone tree is one of the most powerful subjects in landscape photography, offering simplicity, isolation and a strong sense of character. Set against an expansive landscape or dramatic sky, a single tree can become a natural focal point, drawing the viewer into the image while suggesting stories of resilience, solitude and the passage of time.

albums.title: Sea Scapes
albums.blurb: Seascape photography can be both challenging and rewarding, demanding patience, careful timing and a close eye on the changing conditions. Tides, weather, waves and light can transform the same location from one moment to the next, while capturing the movement and power of the sea requires both creativity and technical skill. When everything comes together, however, the results can be truly dramatic and unforgettable.

albums.title: Whalley Village
albums.blurb: Whalley is a historic Lancashire village rich in character, with the River Calder, traditional buildings and the magnificent ruins of Whalley Abbey providing a wonderful sense of place. The abbey’s ancient stonework, peaceful grounds and surrounding village offer a wealth of photographic opportunities, capturing both the beauty of the landscape and the history that has shaped this special corner of the Ribble Valley.

albums.title: Padstow
albums.blurb: Padstow is a charming Cornish harbour town, full of character, colour and photographic interest. From the working harbour and traditional fishing boats to the narrow streets and dramatic coastline nearby, the area offers a wonderful variety of subjects. The changing tides and coastal light make every visit an opportunity to capture something new.

albums.title: St Ives
albums.blurb: St Ives is a wonderfully photogenic coastal town, where golden beaches, turquoise waters and a maze of narrow streets provide endless inspiration. The changing light, colourful harbour and dramatic Cornish coastline make it a perfect location for capturing everything from intimate details to sweeping seascapes.

albums.title: St Michael’s Mount
albums.blurb: St Michael’s Mount is one of Cornwall’s most iconic and dramatic photographic locations, rising from the sea just off the coast at Marazion. The changing tides, which reveal and cover the historic causeway, create endless opportunities for composition, while the castle and its reflections provide a striking focal point. From dramatic sunsets to moody coastal weather, St Michael’s Mount is a location that never fails to inspire.
